rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 8 (sensors moved forward to y 0.06, otherwise the iteration 6 controller) is the best raced design at 686.6, up from 604.0. Oval and s-bend both finished 20 of 20, with s-bend steering_oscillation down from 0.397 to 0.314 and oval from 0.356 to 0.240. Slalom still ends off track in 20 of 20 runs, but progress rose from 0.33 to 0.40. Slalom line_loss_events rose from 1.0 to 1.15, so line loss did not fall. The Evaluator's rule for this case is met on its progress branch (slalom progress above 0.33 with oval near 18 of 20, now 20 of 20). It says to keep sensor y 0.06 and test base_speed 1.4 as the next single change. Oval and s-bend finish times (about 2.0 and 2.2 s) leave time headroom under the 3 s limit, so a speed step is affordable there.

Change. From iteration 8, one value: controller.base_speed 1.2 to 1.4. Sensor geometry (all five at y 0.06, x -0.03 to 0.03, size 0.016), kp 1.5, ki 0.02, kd 0.6, sensor_weights and line_loss last_direction are unchanged, so the result is attributable to speed.

Expected result. Oval and s-bend finish times should drop by roughly 15 percent, adding a few points each through the time term. Slalom progress should hold or rise, since the robot covers more ground before the off-track limit. Risk: the faster robot may leave the track sooner on slalom's tight bends, and at higher speed the 2 percent motor mismatch and sensor noise have more effect. If oval or s-bend finishes fall below 18 of 20, or slalom progress falls below 0.33, revert base_speed to 1.2. If s-bend or oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.4, revert too.

Hypotheses. H1: at y 0.06 the robot now tracks well enough on oval and s-bend that speed is the next limit there, so 1.4 saves time without losing finishes. H2: slalom off-track events are caused by tight-bend overshoot at speed, so 1.4 will not fix slalom and may raise its line-loss count. Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, so the speed effect can be separated per track.
